message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph unless posted otherwise.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 25 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑seat child safety seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers: 0.04 %.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At four‑way stops, the first vehicle to arrive has priority. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or low visibility. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing requires a valid license and proper equipment. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• In Texas, stopping is required in both directions. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in some counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Vehicle Inspection** | • All vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: 30/60/30 (bodily injury per person, bodily injury per accident, property damage). | ### How to Find More Detailed Information - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official rules, regulations, and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Driver licensing, DUI enforcement, and vehicle registration details. If you need specific statutes, court cases, or recent changes, let me know!
